cpu.name: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X
cpu.note: 16-core/32-thread. Best pure render/encode throughput in this list.

cpu.name: Intel Core Ultra 9 285K
cpu.note: Strong Quick Sync hardware decode -- a good alternative if you're heavy on H.264/H.265.

gpu.name: NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti 16GB
gpu.note: Budget-friendly 16GB card, solid 4K H.264/H.265 entry point.

gpu.name: NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti 16GB
gpu.note: Sweet spot for 4K grading/effects; most mature GPU-accelerated path in most NLEs.

gpu.name: NVIDIA RTX 5080 16GB
gpu.note: Faster compute for heavy noise reduction/compositing, same 16GB ceiling as the 5070 Ti.

gpu.name: NVIDIA RTX 5090 32GB
gpu.note: For 6K-8K RAW or heavy multicam grading. Overkill below that.

ram.name: 64GB DDR5 kit (2x32GB)
ram.note: Recommended once you're in 4K RAW or multicam territory.

ram.name: 128GB DDR5 kit (2x64GB)
ram.note: Heavy multicam/RAW plus other creative apps open at the same time.

storage.name: 2TB PCIe4 NVMe SSD
storage.note: Great as a dedicated scratch/media drive -- don't edit off your OS drive.

storage.name: 4TB PCIe4 NVMe SSD
storage.note: More headroom for a full documentary project's worth of raw footage.

storage.name: 2TB Thunderbolt/USB4 NVMe enclosure + drive
storage.note: Portable option for footage brought back from a shoot.
